items.claim: The vision-transport frame phrase is printed with its prefixed preposition and then counted over three verses, MT 1:1, MT 8:3 and MT 40:2, but MT 1:1 carries the construct pair alone, מַרְא֥וֹת אֱלֹהִֽים, with no preposition. The three-verse count is controlled by the construct; the prefixed form stands in two of the three. Every other Hebrew fact in the unit holds on the bytes.
items.both_sides: Onset side: MT 8:1 carries the sixth-year dateline and the hand idiom in its divine-name-pair form, MT 8:3 the transport, and a pe stands after MT 7:27 behind the seam - all true on the bytes, and together the strongest onset evidence in the book. Close side: a samekh stands after MT 8:6 and the clause promising a further sight turns the scene forward, with no recognition or utterance close; medium_low is the honest level for that pairing. The finding touches neither seam.

suggested_fix.fact: MT 1:1 carries the construct pair without the preposition, so the three-verse frame count is matched on the construct; the prefixed form stands at MT 8:3 and MT 40:2

items.claim: The close at MT 8:13 is described as having no Masoretic paragraph evidence at all, but the nearest such evidence is the samekh standing after MT 8:14, one verse past the close: the enclosing closed section runs MT 8:7 through MT 8:14 and does not break where this unit breaks. Separately, the repeated clause that carries the close, ע֣וֹד תָּשׁ֥וּב תִּרְאֶ֛ה at MT 8:13 answering וְעוֹד֙ תָּשׁ֣וּב תִּרְאֶ֔ה at MT 8:6, is Masoretic text and not translation-layer material, so calling it tier-4-adjacent understates the layer it belongs to.
items.both_sides: Onset side: MT 8:7 is a transport verse and a samekh stands immediately behind it after MT 8:6, so the onset is well corroborated. Close side: the repeated clause is real Hebrew evidence, which makes the close stronger than the unit claims for it, while the section running on to MT 8:14 makes it weaker by one verse; the two roughly offset and medium holds. On the mark-absence check raised against this unit: the statement is scoped to MT 8:7-8:13 and is true there — the samekh the check points at stands after MT 8:6, outside the span, and the unit discloses it twice. The check does not stand.

suggested_fix.fact: the samekh standing after MT 8:14 places the enclosing closed section at MT 8:7-8:14, one verse past this close; and the repeated clause carrying the close is Masoretic text, not translation-layer material

items.claim: Two mark statements are wrong. The unit's note speaks of a paseq already disclosed at MT 8:14, but the disjunctive-stroke record carries no paseq anywhere in MT 8:14-8:18 — in this chapter it stands at MT 8:1, MT 8:3, MT 8:6 and MT 8:10 only — and the mark after MT 8:14 is a samekh, which the unit cites correctly elsewhere. And the rejected shorter span of MT 8:14-8:15 is described as stopping on that samekh, which it cannot: the samekh falls between MT 8:14 and MT 8:15, inside such a span, so the span that mark would actually close is MT 8:14 alone.
items.both_sides: Onset side: MT 8:14 is a transport verse, but the samekh stands after it, so the Masoretic evidence at this seam supports a close at MT 8:14 rather than an onset there, and the closed section that mark opens runs MT 8:15 through MT 9:3. Close side: MT 8:18 carries no mark and the section runs past it into the next chapter, so the close rests on the wrath declaration and on the fresh cry opening MT 9:1. The span holds on the two transport verses at MT 8:14 and MT 8:16 and on that content close, but the mark evidence points the other way on the onset side and the unit's weighing of it is mis-stated.

suggested_fix.fact: the record carries no paseq in MT 8:14-8:18; the mark after MT 8:14 is a samekh, and the closed section it opens runs to MT 9:3, so the span a mark-driven rival would close is MT 8:14 alone

items.claim: The stated ground for rejecting a cut after MT 9:3 — that the command sequence runs on to MT 9:11 with no address or addressee change — is false on the bytes. The addressee is the man in linen at MT 9:4 (וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אלו), shifts to the six at MT 9:5 (וּלְאֵ֨לֶּה֙ אָמַ֣ר בְּאָזְנַ֔י), to them at MT 9:7 (וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֲלֵיהֶ֜ם), and to the prophet at MT 9:9 (וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֗י).
items.both_sides: The rival cut after MT 9:3 now has both arms it needs: a samekh stands after MT 9:3 and another after MT 9:11, so the closed section is exactly MT 9:4-9:11, and the addressee shifts repeatedly inside it. Against the cut: the cry at MT 9:1 opens the executioners' scene, MT 9:2-9:3 are its setup and the glory's rise there is preparatory rather than a new scene, and a mark informs a boundary without deciding it alone. The span is defensible and the whole-chapter cap already holds the level at medium_low; what must change is the reason given for setting the rival aside.

suggested_fix.fact: the addressee shifts inside MT 9:4-9:11 — the man in linen at MT 9:4, the six at MT 9:5, them at MT 9:7, the prophet at MT 9:9 — so the rival cut after MT 9:3 is set aside on scene continuity and on the rule that a mark informs without deciding, not on an unbroken addressee

items.claim: MT 10:4 is called the first stage of the glory's exit, but MT 9:3 already narrates the same movement from the cherub to the threshold of the house: וּכְב֣וֹד אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל נַעֲלָה֙ מֵעַ֤ל ... עָלָ֔יו אֶ֖ל מִפְתַּ֣ן. The nine-verse count for the divine-name form is correct, because that count is matched on the form and MT 9:3 uses the God-of-Israel title instead; it is the word first that the bytes do not carry.
items.both_sides: Onset side: the samekh standing after MT 9:11 sits immediately behind MT 10:1, and the open section it starts runs on to MT 11:1; MT 10:1 itself carries no formula and no transport verb, so the scene change is argued from the glory's movement. Close side: MT 10:8 carries no mark and the seam rests on the errand being finished before sustained description begins. The correction weakens MT 10:4 as a fresh-scene anchor, since the threshold movement is already told in the preceding chapter, but neither seam moves. On the mark-absence check raised against this unit: the statement is about MT chapter 10, which carries no paragraph mark at all, and the samekh the check points at stands after MT 9:11, which this unit discloses in its own evidence. The check does not stand.

suggested_fix.fact: MT 9:3 already records the glory going up from the cherub to the threshold of the house under the God-of-Israel title, so MT 10:4 is the first verse of the divine-name-form arc rather than the first stage of the exit

items.claim: The exclusivity that certifies this unit is false on the bytes. The wheel vocabulary does recur outside MT 10:6-17 and MT 1:15-21: the wheel word stands at MT 3:13 (הָאוֹפַנִּ֖ים), MT 10:19 (וְהָאֽוֹפַנִּ֖ים) and MT 11:22 (וְהָאֽוֹפַנִּ֖ים), and the whirling-wheel word at MT 10:2 (לַגַּלְגַּ֜ל), MT 23:24 (וְגַלְגַּל֙) and MT 26:10 (וְגַלְגַּ֜ל). Two of those, MT 10:2 and MT 10:19, lie inside the units on either side of this one, which is the opposite of the lexical self-containment the unit rests on. The unit states in the same breath that no formula marks its onset, so this claim is its only affirmative ground.
items.both_sides: Onset side: MT 10:9 opens with the same looking-and-behold clause as MT 10:1, carries no formula and no mark, and the preceding close at MT 10:8 has none either; the whole chapter sits inside one Masoretic section running from MT 10:1 to MT 11:1, so no mark bears on either seam. Close side: MT 10:17 ends the description with its summary clause and MT 10:18 resumes narrated action with the glory going out. Both seams therefore rest on the alternation between narrated action and sustained description alone — a real signal, and why the span can stand at its already-low level — but the lexical argument offered to reinforce them does not survive the bytes and must be withdrawn rather than reworded.

suggested_fix.fact: the wheel vocabulary crosses both adjacent seams, the whirling-wheel word at MT 10:2 and the wheel word at MT 10:19, and it also stands at MT 3:13, MT 11:22, MT 23:24 and MT 26:10, so the ground for this unit is the alternation between narrated action and sustained description, not lexical exclusivity

items.claim: A pe stands after MT 11:1, one verse past this unit's close, so the enclosing open section runs MT 10:1 through MT 11:1 and the Masoretic paragraph break falls at MT 11:1/11:2, not at MT 10:22/11:1. The unit says only that the chapter carries no mark; the nearest paragraph evidence to its close seam is real, points one verse later, and is not disclosed.
items.both_sides: Onset side: MT 10:18 resumes narrated action with the glory going out from the threshold while MT 10:17 closes a description, and no mark bears on that seam. Close side: the Chebar identification at MT 10:20 and MT 10:22 closes the cherubim's identity question and MT 11:1 is a transport verse opening a scene with participants absent from MT 10:18-22 — but the pe after MT 11:1 groups that verse with what precedes it, so the Masoretic layer would put the break one verse later. The seam holds, because a seam inside this vision sits on a transport verse and a mark informs a boundary without deciding it alone; the counter-signal belongs in the record beside the content argument.

unresolved_uncertainty.what: The witness is a single manuscript tradition. Every paragraph mark, disjunctive stroke, ketiv/qere site and editorial note cited here rests on that one witness, and setumah is not treated as equal to petuchah.
unresolved_uncertainty.why_it_matters: Each mark finding above informs a seam and none decides one; a second witness could change the paragraph picture at MT 8:14, MT 9:3 and MT 11:1 that three of these findings rest on.

unresolved_uncertainty.what: The printed device form for the vision-transport frame carries a preposition that MT 1:1 does not — the same shape as the already-retained low where a hand idiom is printed in a form one of its seven verses does not carry. This second instance is not recorded in anything I read.
unresolved_uncertainty.why_it_matters: A later lane re-deriving the count from the printed string gets 2 rather than 3 and may open a finding against a correct count, which is the churn the first retained low was recorded to prevent.

unresolved_uncertainty.what: The retained-lows record binds the toolkit at a digest that no longer matches the file, and the current toolkit already prints the one-clause cure that record offered.
unresolved_uncertainty.why_it_matters: The cure appears to have been folded in as that record permitted, but the binding was not refreshed, so the record no longer proves which bytes it accepted.

unresolved_uncertainty.what: Whether the wheel description stands as its own unit or as texture inside the material on either side is left open by the book's ruled strategy, and with its lexical ground withdrawn the span rests on the narration-versus-description alternation alone.
unresolved_uncertainty.why_it_matters: It is the weakest-anchored seam pair in this cluster and a merge cannot be ruled out from this lens alone; the level already sits at the floor, which is the honest record of that.

Every file I opened was named by its exact path in my brief, my launch message, my own global policy, or the ledger my brief names, and each was opened by that exact path. I created my private scratch subdirectory with mkdir -p and wrote this deliverable directly to the path my launch message named, with no existence check against that directory or any other.
